readings.summary: The vendor group wizard lowercases 'request' for what is otherwise the same Applies To value.
readings.sourceQuote: Select the Payment request document type for which to calculate VAT for vendor groups.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Prefer the capitalised 'Payment Request' when selecting the Applies To value - corpus-wide it is the form in 135 files against 2 for 'Payment request' - and match case-insensitively so either rendering resolves. Never compare the option string byte-for-byte across the two wizards and never fail a step on the casing alone. Applies to both expenseTypeGroupAppliesTo and vendorGroupAppliesTo, which is why this attaches to no single field.
configContradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW to a probable typo rather than two option values. Hypothesis: a shift key missed while copying one wizard topic from the other - the two sentences are otherwise word-for-word twins differing only in the trailing noun ('for expense type groups' / 'for vendor groups'), and corpus-wide 'Payment Request' appears in 135 files while 'Payment request' appears in 2 (this vendor-group topic and process-overview-payment-request-import-8b42995f.md). CORRECTION to the raw record's note: the sentence 'The Applies To setting also appears as a column on the Expense Type Groups page.' is NOT peculiar to the vendor-group topic - it sits at line 96 of BOTH wizard topics, which is itself evidence of copying. It has no competing reading, so it is recorded here rather than as its own node.

configContradictions.topic: State/Province is optional on the Company Locations add-address form but mandatory in the Purchase Order address import records that create the same rows

readings.summary: The Company Locations add-address field table marks State/Province as optional, so an address typed on the page can be saved with the state or province left blank.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province
    
    (Optional)

readings.summary: The Company Locations topic's own revision history records State/Province being changed TO optional on September 9, 2016, confirming the optional marking is deliberate and dated rather than a table typo. (Source characters: in the file this bullet is written '-   State/Province field now an optional field' with a leading hyphen and three spaces; the quote drops the leading '-   ' so that a bare grep -F does not read it as a command-line option.)
readings.sourceQuote: State/Province field now an optional field

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Bill-to Address (record type 210) import format marks State/Province Required? = Y, so a bill-to address arriving by import must carry a state or province.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province

 | 

Maximum 255 characters

 | 

Y

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Ship-to Address (record type 220) import format likewise marks State/Province Required? = Y for the ship-to twin of the same address record.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province

 | 

Maximum 255 characters

 | 

Y

readings.summary: The linkage the disagreement depends on, stated by the add-address topic itself: the Address Code typed on the Company Locations form is identical to the External ID field of the Purchase Order Bill To and Ship To record sets - so the page and the 210/220 import are two entry paths onto the same address records rather than unrelated stores. This reading takes no side; it establishes that the two sides collide.
readings.sourceQuote: This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat State/Province as OPTIONAL when driving the Add New Ship To / Bill To Location window - do not fail a step because the field is blank, and do not assert a required-field error if it is left empty. Treat it as REQUIRED when generating or validating a Purchase Order 210/220 import row: always populate it there. If a single value set feeds both paths, populate State/Province unconditionally, because that satisfies both accounts; never assert the reverse (that a blank one will be rejected on screen).
configContradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the two rules belong to two different entry paths rather than to one stored constraint - the browser form relaxed the rule in 2016 while the batch importer's record specification was never re-cut, so the same logical address column is validated differently depending on whether it arrives through the UI or the feed file. A second, weaker hypothesis is that the import requirement is a file-format (positional column) requirement rather than a value requirement, but the corpus never says so.

readings.summary: The Company Locations add-address field table marks Name as required - and elsewhere in the same table Name is the value searched on when picking a Bill To or Ship To address.

    (Required)

readings.summary: The linkage the disagreement depends on, stated by the add-address topic itself: the Address Code typed on the Company Locations form is identical to the External ID field of the Purchase Order Bill To and Ship To record sets - so the page and the 210/220 import are two entry paths onto the same address records rather than unrelated stores. This reading takes no side; it establishes that the two sides collide.

configContradictions.topic: Country Code length is stated as exactly '2 characters' in the 210 record and as 'Maximum 2 characters' in the otherwise identical 220 record

readings.summary: The Bill-to Address (record type 210) import format defines Country Code as exactly 2 characters - a fixed width, not a ceiling.
readings.sourceQuote:
Country Code

 | 

2 characters

readings.summary: The Ship-to Address (record type 220) import format defines the same column as a maximum of 2 characters, which would also admit a 1-character value.
readings.sourceQuote:
Country Code

 | 

Maximum 2 characters

readings.summary: The Company Locations add-address topic states no length rule for a value typed on the page; its Country Code cell gives a 2-character ISO-code rule only for the import template.
readings.sourceQuote: If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Always emit exactly two characters for Country Code - a 2-character value satisfies 'exactly 2', 'maximum 2' and the ISO instruction simultaneously, so it is the only value shape that is safe under all three accounts. Do not build a validator that ACCEPTS a 1-character country code on the strength of the 220 wording, and do not build one that rejects the 220 record for stating a maximum.
configContradictions.notes: Hypothesis: a documentation-editing artefact rather than a product difference - the 210 and 220 tables are field-for-field twins and the Definition column diverges only here (the External ID and Name Description prose also differ between the two files), which suggests the twins were edited separately rather than that the importer behaves differently per record type. Kind note: the enum has no 'constraint' member; 'requirement' is used as the nearest fit for a field-width rule stated two ways.

configContradictions.topic: Three different guide titles are cited for Company Locations - a Setup Guide and a User Guide under the same product prefix, plus a third 'Shared:' title that may be a different guide - and none of the three is present in this corpus

readings.summary: The Tax Service topic cites a third, differently-prefixed title - 'Shared: Locations Setup Guide' - under the Shared: prefix and with 'Company' dropped. The corpus nowhere states that this is the same document as the two Company Locations titles, so it MAY be a different guide.
readings.sourceQuote: More Information: For more information, refer to the Shared: Locations Setup Guide.

configContradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not resolve cross-references by exact title match, and do not treat a missing 'Concur Invoice: Company Locations User Guide' as a broken link - all three strings are live in the corpus and none of the three documents is in it. If the automation surfaces a doc pointer to the operator, surface the string as written in the topic it came from rather than normalising to one canonical title.

The third title drops 'Company' and carries the 'Shared:' prefix, and Locations is a shared SAP Concur feature in its own right - so this node does NOT assert that all three name one document. Hypothesis: the guide was renamed over time (Setup Guide -> User Guide) and a separate shared-feature guide exists alongside it, with the older cross-references never re-cut. Stated as a hypothesis; the corpus contains none of the three targets, so neither the drift nor the identity can be confirmed from inside it. Cross-reference (NOT merged): the List Management node records the same 'Shared:' vs 'Concur Invoice:' prefix drift on a different guide - different documents, different citing topics - so they stay two nodes.

configContradictions.topic: Three accounts of the parent menu for Company Locations - an 'Invoice Processing Admin' menu, 'Administration > Invoice', and 'Invoice Admin' - including one topic whose prose disagrees with its own numbered steps

readings.summary: The numbered steps in that same topic never mention Invoice Processing Admin; they end by selecting Company Locations from a left menu rather than by walking a breadcrumb chain.
readings.sourceQuote: 2.  Select Company Locations (left menu).

Treat the absence of an 'Invoice Processing Admin' node as expected, not as a failed step.
